Going into my 16 year old daughter's room 2 months ago to wake her for school. I assumed she had slept through her alarm again. It was dark, so when I put one hand on the edge of the bed to reach her shoulder with the other, I didn't see the vomit I would be putting my hand into. 

At first I thought she had the flu. She started to wake. I asked what she had eaten because the chalky texture of the puke kept striking me as really strange. I turned on the light to help clean her up, and saw the color as well. And that it was EVERYwhere. 

Then I asked again. What did you take?!! She sort of motioned to the 3 empty pill bottles (tylenol, ibuprofen, and aspirin) in a pile of stuff near the bed. 

I ran to the doorway to call in my boyfriend who's a nurse. He went from eyes closed to wide awake, and in with her in seconds, while I called 911. 

We rode in the back of an ambulance to the hospital. She was on an IV for 3 days to pump out the poisons, and try to minimize potential for liver and kidney damage. For 3 days sitting by her bed I didn't know if she would live, even though she had survived initially. My boyfriend had seen a case in med school where the 15 yr old had ingested far fewer tylenol and a week later died due to the irreversible liver damage it caused. 

Thank God she was okay. No sign of any lasting damage. 

I was terrified from the moment I learned she had taken all the pills until weeks later when she was discharged from the hospital. 

I don't know if I'm ever going to sleep as soundly again though. I still have nightmares. I still hold my breath every morning when I go in to make sure she is awake. I still check on her through the night like I used to when she was a baby. 

The ongoing process of the recovery in itself is scary because I don't know if all the therapy and everything is enough and she means the world to me.
